products.name: Sualkuchi Muga Mekhela Chador — Natural Gold
products.shortDescription: A two-piece Muga Mekhela Chador in undyed golden yarn, handwoven on Sualkuchi looms.
products.description: Woven in Sualkuchi, the weaving village on the north bank of the Brahmaputra where Muga has been worked for generations. The yarn is undyed — the deep honey gold is the fibre's own colour, drawn from the Muga silkworm and nothing else. Both the mekhela and the chador are woven as a matched pair on the same loom so the sheen runs continuously across the drape. A fine kesa border edges the chador, and the anchal carries a narrow woven band rather than applied work. Muga is famously durable and its lustre deepens each time it is washed. Dry clean for the first two years, then a gentle cold hand wash. Store folded in unbleached muslin, away from direct light.
products.metaTitle: Sualkuchi Muga Mekhela Chador — Natural Gold | Meghali's Silk
products.metaDescription: A two-piece Muga Mekhela Chador in undyed golden yarn, handwoven on Sualkuchi looms.

products.name: Muga Mekhela Chador — Ivory Pat Border
products.shortDescription: Golden Muga body with a woven ivory Pat border — the classic Assamese contrast.
products.description: A Muga drape given an ivory Pat silk border, the pairing Assamese weavers have used for as long as both fibres have been on the same loom. The golden ground stays undyed; only the border yarn changes, so the contrast is a matter of fibre rather than dye. Woven to order in Sualkuchi over roughly three weeks. The chador is finished with a hand-rolled hem and the mekhela comes unpleated so it can be set to your height. Dry clean recommended. Press on the reverse with a cool iron and a cotton cloth between.
products.metaTitle: Muga Mekhela Chador — Ivory Pat Border | Meghali's Silk
products.metaDescription: Golden Muga body with a woven ivory Pat border — the classic Assamese contrast.

products.name: Muga Mekhela Chador — Kingkhap Motif
products.shortDescription: Muga Mekhela Chador carrying the kingkhap, the most demanding of the Assamese loom motifs.
products.description: The kingkhap is the motif Sualkuchi weavers are measured by — a dense, geometric figure lifted thread by thread on the loom rather than embroidered afterwards. On this drape it runs across the anchal and repeats as a small buta through the body. Roughly six weeks of loom time. The Muga yarn is undyed golden throughout; the motif reads darker only because of how the lifted threads catch light. A piece intended for weddings, Bihu and the occasions that get photographed. Dry clean only. Rest it a day between wears and store folded in muslin.
products.metaTitle: Muga Mekhela Chador — Kingkhap Motif | Meghali's Silk
products.metaDescription: Muga Mekhela Chador carrying the kingkhap, the most demanding of the Assamese loom motifs.

products.name: Muga Mekhela Chador — Jaapi Buta
products.shortDescription: A lighter Muga drape scattered with the jaapi buta, the woven Assamese sunhat motif.
products.description: The jaapi — the bamboo-and-leaf sunhat carried across Assam — reduced to a small repeating buta across the body of the chador. It is a quieter piece than our kingkhap drapes: fewer lifted threads, less loom time, and a lighter hand as a result. The Muga is undyed and takes on the warm gold that shows up best in daylight. Suited to daytime functions and to office wear through Bihu week. Dry clean. A cool iron on the reverse is enough to settle creases.
products.metaTitle: Muga Mekhela Chador — Jaapi Buta | Meghali's Silk
products.metaDescription: A lighter Muga drape scattered with the jaapi buta, the woven Assamese sunhat motif.

products.name: Muga Mekhela Chador — Everyday Weave
products.shortDescription: Plain-bodied Muga with a narrow woven border — the drape our weavers wear themselves.
products.description: The simplest Muga drape we make: a plain body, a narrow two-inch border, no buta. It uses less yarn and far less loom time than our motif pieces, which is the whole reason it costs what it does. What you get is unchanged — the same undyed Sualkuchi Muga, the same fibre that outlasts the person who buys it. Weavers in the village keep a plain drape like this for themselves and wear it for years. Dry clean for the first season, then a cold hand wash with a mild detergent suits it well.
products.metaTitle: Muga Mekhela Chador — Everyday Weave | Meghali's Silk
products.metaDescription: Plain-bodied Muga with a narrow woven border — the drape our weavers wear themselves.

products.name: Pat Silk Mekhela Chador — Ivory & Gold
products.shortDescription: Ivory Pat silk with a gold zari border — the drape worn at Bihu across Assam.
products.description: Pat is Assam's mulberry silk: brighter and finer than Muga, and traditionally kept in ivory and white. This is the drape you see on stage at Bihu — an ivory body, a gold zari border and anchal, nothing else competing with it. Handwoven in Sualkuchi. The chador is generous enough to pleat properly at the shoulder, and the mekhela is supplied unpleated. Pat holds a crisp fall straight off the loom and softens over the first few wears. Dry clean. Store away from damp, which is what dulls zari.
products.metaTitle: Pat Silk Mekhela Chador — Ivory & Gold | Meghali's Silk
products.metaDescription: Ivory Pat silk with a gold zari border — the drape worn at Bihu across Assam.

products.name: Pat Silk Mekhela Chador — Deep Crimson
products.shortDescription: Pat silk taken into a deep crimson, with a contrast gold border along the anchal.
products.description: Pat takes dye more evenly than Muga does, which is why colour work in Assamese silk almost always happens here. This drape is dyed a deep crimson and bordered in gold, a pairing that reads as festive without tipping into bridal. Handwoven in Sualkuchi on a fly-shuttle loom. The dye is set before weaving, so the colour sits inside the yarn rather than on top of it and will not crock onto a blouse. Dry clean only. Keep it out of prolonged sun, which lifts any deep dye over time.
products.metaTitle: Pat Silk Mekhela Chador — Deep Crimson | Meghali's Silk
products.metaDescription: Pat silk taken into a deep crimson, with a contrast gold border along the anchal.

products.name: Pat Silk Mekhela Chador — Mayur Buta
products.shortDescription: Ivory Pat with the mayur — the peacock buta — lifted across body and anchal.
products.description: The mayur buta is one of the older figures in the Assamese loom vocabulary, and one of the few that reads clearly at a distance. Here it repeats in gold across an ivory Pat ground and gathers into a wider band at the anchal. Around four weeks on the loom in Sualkuchi. Pat gives the motif more definition than Muga would, because the yarn is finer and the ground is pale. A wedding-guest drape rather than a bridal one. Dry clean. Fold along the woven lines and rest it in muslin between wears.
products.metaTitle: Pat Silk Mekhela Chador — Mayur Buta | Meghali's Silk
products.metaDescription: Ivory Pat with the mayur — the peacock buta — lifted across body and anchal.

products.name: Pat Silk Mekhela Chador — Pastel Blush
products.shortDescription: A light Pat drape in soft blush with a tonal border — for daytime, not the mandap.
products.description: A deliberately understated Pat drape: a blush ground, a border dyed a half-shade deeper, and no zari at all. It reads well in daylight and photographs without glare, which is more than can be said for most silk in an Assamese summer. Woven light so it stays comfortable through a long function. Handwoven in Sualkuchi. Dry clean is safest for the dye, though the weave itself is robust. Store folded in muslin, since pale silk picks up marks from wood and cardboard.
products.metaTitle: Pat Silk Mekhela Chador — Pastel Blush | Meghali's Silk
products.metaDescription: A light Pat drape in soft blush with a tonal border — for daytime, not the mandap.

products.name: Eri Silk Mekhela Chador — Undyed Natural
products.shortDescription: Undyed Eri in its own oatmeal colour — matte, warm and made for wearing often.
products.description: Eri is the quiet member of the Assamese silk family. The cocoon is left to open before the yarn is reeled, so the filament is spun rather than drawn, and the cloth comes out matte and slightly textured instead of shiny. It is warmer than it looks and forgiving in a way Muga and Pat are not: it creases less, it hangs softer, and it wants to be worn rather than kept. Handwoven undyed in the natural oatmeal of the fibre. Gentle cold hand wash, dry in shade. It softens with every wash, which is the point.
products.metaTitle: Eri Silk Mekhela Chador — Undyed Natural | Meghali's Silk
products.metaDescription: Undyed Eri in its own oatmeal colour — matte, warm and made for wearing often.

products.name: Eri Mekhela Chador — Madder Rust
products.shortDescription: Eri dyed with madder root to a warm rust, with an undyed natural border.
products.description: Madder root gives Eri a rust that synthetic dye never quite reaches — slightly uneven, warmer in some lights than others, and settled rather than bright. The border is left undyed so the two states of the same fibre sit next to each other. Dyed and handwoven in Assam. Because this is a natural dye the shade shifts a little between batches and will mellow over years of wear; that is the nature of the material, not a fault. Cold hand wash separately for the first two washes, then dry flat in shade.
products.metaTitle: Eri Mekhela Chador — Madder Rust | Meghali's Silk
products.metaDescription: Eri dyed with madder root to a warm rust, with an undyed natural border.

products.name: Nuni Silk Mekhela Chador — Tea Green
products.shortDescription: Nuni silk, the lighter Assamese mulberry yarn, in a soft tea green with a woven stripe.
products.description: Nuni is reared on a different mulberry variety from Pat and reels finer, giving a cloth that is lighter in the hand and slightly less lustrous. It suits a drape you want to wear through a working day. The tea green here is a nod to the gardens the yarn travels past on its way to the loom, and a narrow tonal stripe runs the length of the mekhela. Handwoven in Assam. Dry clean, or a careful cold hand wash. Press on the reverse with a cloth between.
products.metaTitle: Nuni Silk Mekhela Chador — Tea Green | Meghali's Silk
products.metaDescription: Nuni silk, the lighter Assamese mulberry yarn, in a soft tea green with a woven stripe.

products.name: Muga Silk Saree — Assam Golden
products.shortDescription: Six yards of undyed Muga with a woven border — the drape, in saree form.
products.description: The same Sualkuchi Muga we weave into Mekhela Chador, run to six and a quarter yards for those who prefer a saree. Undyed golden yarn throughout, a woven border on both edges, and a plain anchal finished with a fine band. Muga's reputation for lasting is not marketing: pieces of it are handed down, and the sheen improves rather than fades with washing. Comes with an unstitched Muga blouse piece. Dry clean for the first two years, then a gentle cold hand wash. Store folded in unbleached muslin.
products.metaTitle: Muga Silk Saree — Assam Golden | Meghali's Silk
products.metaDescription: Six yards of undyed Muga with a woven border — the drape, in saree form.

products.name: Muga Silk Saree — Red Kingkhap Border
products.shortDescription: Golden Muga with a crimson kingkhap border and a fully figured anchal.
products.description: A statement Muga saree: the body stays undyed gold, and the kingkhap is worked in crimson along both borders before opening out across the whole anchal. All of it is lifted on the loom — there is no embroidery on this saree anywhere. Roughly five weeks of loom time in Sualkuchi. It is heavier than our plain Muga sarees and drapes accordingly, so allow time to set the pleats. Supplied with an unstitched blouse piece. Dry clean only. Rest it a day between wears.
products.metaTitle: Muga Silk Saree — Red Kingkhap Border | Meghali's Silk
products.metaDescription: Golden Muga with a crimson kingkhap border and a fully figured anchal.

products.name: Muga Silk Saree — Fine Gos Buta
products.shortDescription: A light Muga saree with the gos buta, the small woven tree motif, repeating through the body.
products.description: Gos means tree, and the gos buta is the small stylised figure Assamese weavers scatter across a plain ground when a saree needs interest but not weight. Here it repeats in the same undyed golden yarn as the body, so it shows as texture rather than contrast — you see it properly only up close or in raking light. Woven lighter than our bordered Muga sarees and easy to wear for a full day. Handwoven in Sualkuchi with an unstitched blouse piece. Dry clean, and use a cool iron on the reverse.
products.metaTitle: Muga Silk Saree — Fine Gos Buta | Meghali's Silk
products.metaDescription: A light Muga saree with the gos buta, the small woven tree motif, repeating through the body.

products.name: Pat Silk Saree — Ivory Zari
products.shortDescription: Ivory Pat silk with a gold zari border and anchal — the Assamese festive standard.
products.description: Ivory and gold is the combination Assam reaches for at Bihu, at weddings, at anything that calls for silk. This saree keeps to it strictly: an ivory Pat ground, a gold zari border on both edges, and an anchal of woven zari bands. Handwoven in Sualkuchi. Pat has a brighter, finer surface than Muga and holds a crisp pleat, which is why it photographs so well under lights. Comes with an unstitched blouse piece. Dry clean, and keep it dry — damp is what tarnishes zari.
products.metaTitle: Pat Silk Saree — Ivory Zari | Meghali's Silk
products.metaDescription: Ivory Pat silk with a gold zari border and anchal — the Assamese festive standard.

products.name: Pat Silk Saree — Indigo Miri Border
products.shortDescription: Indigo Pat silk edged with the miri, the geometric band borrowed from Mising weaving.
products.description: The miri band — tight, angular, repeating — comes from the Mising weaving tradition of upper Assam and has long since crossed into Sualkuchi work. Set against an indigo Pat ground it gives a saree that reads as contemporary without being untraditional. The indigo is dyed at the yarn stage. Handwoven in Assam and supplied with an unstitched blouse piece. Dry clean. Keep indigo out of long sun, and wash separately if you ever do wash it, as deep dyes can bleed on first contact with water.
products.metaTitle: Pat Silk Saree — Indigo Miri Border | Meghali's Silk
products.metaDescription: Indigo Pat silk edged with the miri, the geometric band borrowed from Mising weaving.

products.name: Nuni Silk Saree — Warm Sand
products.shortDescription: A light Nuni silk saree in warm sand, woven plain with a tonal border.
products.description: Nuni reels finer than Pat and weaves up lighter, which makes it the sensible choice for a saree you intend to wear through the humid months. This one is kept plain — a warm sand ground, a border a shade deeper, no zari and no buta. It takes a soft fall rather than a crisp one. Handwoven in Assam and supplied with an unstitched blouse piece. Dry clean or cold hand wash. Dry in shade and press on the reverse.
products.metaTitle: Nuni Silk Saree — Warm Sand | Meghali's Silk
products.metaDescription: A light Nuni silk saree in warm sand, woven plain with a tonal border.

products.name: Eri Silk Shawl — Undyed Ivory
products.shortDescription: A handspun Eri shawl in undyed ivory, warm enough for a Guwahati winter evening.
products.description: Eri is spun rather than reeled, which gives it a soft, slightly irregular surface and a warmth closer to fine wool than to silk. This shawl is left undyed in the fibre's own pale ivory, with a plain hand-knotted fringe at both ends and no border. It is the piece to keep in a bag from November onwards. Handspun and handwoven in Assam. Gentle cold hand wash with a mild detergent, dry flat in shade. Eri gets softer and slightly fuller with each wash.
products.metaTitle: Eri Silk Shawl — Undyed Ivory | Meghali's Silk
products.metaDescription: A handspun Eri shawl in undyed ivory, warm enough for a Guwahati winter evening.

products.name: Eri Silk Stole — Madder Rust
products.shortDescription: A lighter Eri stole in madder-dyed rust, cut narrow for layering.
products.description: The same handspun Eri as our shawls, woven narrower and lighter so it works over a kurta or a coat rather than as a wrap. Dyed with madder root, which settles into a warm, slightly variable rust rather than a flat one. Because the dye is natural, no two lengths come out identically and the colour will mellow over the years. Handwoven in Assam with a short twisted fringe. Cold hand wash separately for the first two washes, then dry flat in shade.
products.metaTitle: Eri Silk Stole — Madder Rust | Meghali's Silk
products.metaDescription: A lighter Eri stole in madder-dyed rust, cut narrow for layering.

products.name: Eri Silk Shawl — Charcoal Handspun
products.shortDescription: Our heaviest Eri: a dense handspun shawl in charcoal, woven on a pit loom.
products.description: The thickest Eri we stock. The yarn is handspun coarser than usual and woven on a pit loom at a low pick rate, which produces a dense, blanket-weight cloth that still drapes. Dyed a deep charcoal that keeps the fibre's natural irregularity visible rather than hiding it. This is a winter shawl in the plain sense — it takes the place of a jacket. Handspun and handwoven in Assam. Dry clean, or cold hand wash alone and dry flat; do not wring a shawl this heavy.
products.metaTitle: Eri Silk Shawl — Charcoal Handspun | Meghali's Silk
products.metaDescription: Our heaviest Eri: a dense handspun shawl in charcoal, woven on a pit loom.

products.name: Eri Cotton Stole — Everyday Natural
products.shortDescription: Eri blended with cotton for a light everyday stole that washes without ceremony.
products.description: Eri warp, cotton weft — a blend Assamese weavers use for cloth that has to survive daily life. It keeps most of Eri's matte softness while dropping the price and the fuss: this one goes in a cold machine wash on a gentle cycle without complaint. Left undyed in the natural colour of both fibres, with a plain selvedge and no fringe. Handwoven in Assam. The most-repeated purchase in our stole range, usually two or three at a time.
products.metaTitle: Eri Cotton Stole — Everyday Natural | Meghali's Silk
products.metaDescription: Eri blended with cotton for a light everyday stole that washes without ceremony.

products.name: Muga Silk Stole — Natural Gold
products.shortDescription: A full-width Muga stole in undyed gold — the sheen of a Muga drape, worn daily.
products.description: For anyone who wants Muga in their week rather than only at weddings. Undyed golden yarn from the same Sualkuchi looms as our Mekhela Chador, woven to stole width with a fine woven border and a short fringe. It reads as gold in daylight and closer to bronze under indoor light, which is simply how the fibre behaves. Handwoven in Sualkuchi. Dry clean for the first year, then a gentle cold hand wash. Fold rather than hang, and store in muslin.
products.metaTitle: Muga Silk Stole — Natural Gold | Meghali's Silk
products.metaDescription: A full-width Muga stole in undyed gold — the sheen of a Muga drape, worn daily.

products.name: Pat Silk Stole — Ivory Zari Edge
products.shortDescription: Ivory Pat silk with a narrow gold zari edge — the lightest festive layer we make.
products.description: A stole cut from the same ivory Pat we use for our Bihu drapes, with a narrow zari line along both edges and nothing else. It is light enough to sit over a plain kurta without adding bulk, and formal enough to carry a simple outfit through a function. Handwoven in Sualkuchi. Pat holds its crispness, so this stole keeps its shape over a shoulder rather than slumping. Dry clean, and keep it dry — zari dulls in damp storage more than through wear.
products.metaTitle: Pat Silk Stole — Ivory Zari Edge | Meghali's Silk
products.metaDescription: Ivory Pat silk with a narrow gold zari edge — the lightest festive layer we make.

products.name: Muga Silk Blouse Piece — Unstitched
products.shortDescription: A metre of undyed Muga, cut as a blouse piece to match a Muga drape exactly.
products.description: Muga varies subtly from batch to batch, so the surest way to match a blouse to a drape is to cut it from the same yarn. This is one metre of undyed Sualkuchi Muga, wide enough for a standard blouse with sleeves, supplied unstitched so your own tailor can work to your measurements. Buy it alongside a Muga Mekhela Chador or saree and we cut from the nearest available batch. Dry clean the finished blouse. Pre-shrinking is unnecessary; Muga is stable off the loom.
products.metaTitle: Muga Silk Blouse Piece — Unstitched | Meghali's Silk
products.metaDescription: A metre of undyed Muga, cut as a blouse piece to match a Muga drape exactly.

products.name: Pat Silk Blouse — Ready to Wear
products.shortDescription: A ready-stitched Pat silk blouse in ivory, lined and finished to pair with any drape.
products.description: A plain ivory Pat silk blouse, stitched and lined, with a back hook opening and elbow-length sleeves. It is deliberately unadorned so it sits under a figured Mekhela Chador without competing with it. Cut on the trim side, which is standard for blouses meant to be worn with a drape — check the size chart and take the next size up if you are between two. Handwoven Pat from Sualkuchi, stitched in Guwahati. Dry clean, or a careful cold hand wash inside out.
products.metaTitle: Pat Silk Blouse — Ready to Wear | Meghali's Silk
products.metaDescription: A ready-stitched Pat silk blouse in ivory, lined and finished to pair with any drape.

products.name: Eri Silk Running Fabric — Per Metre
products.shortDescription: Undyed handwoven Eri sold by the metre, 44 inches wide, for your own tailoring.
products.description: Plain handwoven Eri from our own looms, sold by the metre at 44 inches usable width. Tailors like it because it cuts cleanly, takes a seam without slipping, and holds a soft structure that suits jackets, kurtas and unlined dresses as readily as blouses. Left undyed, so it also takes a natural dye well if you are working with a dyer. Cut as one continuous length up to five metres. Pre-wash before cutting if the finished garment will be machine washed, since Eri relaxes slightly on first wash.
products.metaTitle: Eri Silk Running Fabric — Per Metre | Meghali's Silk
products.metaDescription: Undyed handwoven Eri sold by the metre, 44 inches wide, for your own tailoring.

products.name: Gamosa Gift Set — Handwoven Pair
products.shortDescription: Two handwoven gamosas, the red-bordered Assamese cloth given as a mark of respect.
products.description: The gamosa is the cloth Assam gives: draped over a guest's shoulder, offered at Bihu, folded onto every household shrine. Ours are handwoven in cotton with the traditional red border and woven buta at both ends, and come as a pair in a plain kraft sleeve. Not silk, and not pretending to be — a gamosa is a cotton cloth by definition, and that is what makes it usable. Machine washable, and it softens quickly. The most common gift order we pack, usually several at once around Bohag Bihu.
products.metaTitle: Gamosa Gift Set — Handwoven Pair | Meghali's Silk
products.metaDescription: Two handwoven gamosas, the red-bordered Assamese cloth given as a mark of respect.

products.name: Muga Silk Cushion Cover — Set of Two
products.shortDescription: Two cushion covers woven from Muga loom ends, with the fibre's own gold sheen.
products.description: Muga is too valuable to waste, so the short lengths left at the end of a drape warp go into pieces like these. Two covers, 16 by 16 inches, in undyed golden Muga with a concealed zip and a plain cotton backing. Because they come from loom ends, the exact shade varies a little between batches, and occasionally between the two covers in a set — that is the honest consequence of using the offcut rather than a fault. Cushion inserts are not included. Dry clean.
products.metaTitle: Muga Silk Cushion Cover — Set of Two | Meghali's Silk
products.metaDescription: Two cushion covers woven from Muga loom ends, with the fibre's own gold sheen.

products.name: Eri Silk Table Runner — Natural
products.shortDescription: A handspun Eri table runner in undyed natural, six feet long with a knotted fringe.
products.description: Six feet of handspun undyed Eri, woven at shawl weight and finished with a hand-knotted fringe at both ends. Eri's matte surface suits a table better than a glossy silk does — it does not throw light back at the room, and it does not slide off the edge. Handwoven in Assam. The natural oatmeal colour sits well on both dark wood and pale linen. Gentle cold hand wash, dry flat in shade; it will soften and full slightly after the first wash, which is normal for handspun Eri.
products.metaTitle: Eri Silk Table Runner — Natural | Meghali's Silk
products.metaDescription: A handspun Eri table runner in undyed natural, six feet long with a knotted fringe.

products.name: Bihu Keepsake Box — Gamosa & Eri Stole
products.shortDescription: A handwoven gamosa and an Eri stole boxed together for Bohag Bihu.
products.description: Our standing Bihu gift: one handwoven gamosa with the traditional red border, and one undyed Eri cotton stole, packed together in a rigid box lined with unbleached muslin and tied with a cotton tape. It is the pairing people in Assam actually give — the gamosa for the gesture, the stole because it gets worn. A blank card goes in the lid for your own message. Assembled and packed to order, so allow a day extra during Bihu week. Care notes for both pieces are printed inside the lid.
products.metaTitle: Bihu Keepsake Box — Gamosa & Eri Stole | Meghali's Silk
products.metaDescription: A handwoven gamosa and an Eri stole boxed together for Bohag Bihu.

products.name: Bridal Muga Mekhela Chador — Kingkhap Gold
products.shortDescription: The full bridal set: undyed Muga worked in kingkhap across mekhela, chador and blouse piece.
products.description: Our heaviest bridal commission. Undyed Sualkuchi Muga throughout, with the kingkhap lifted across the full anchal, repeated as a border on both edges of the mekhela, and carried onto a matching blouse piece cut from the same warp. Around ten weeks on the loom for a single set, worked by one weaver so the motif stays consistent end to end. Supplied with the blouse piece unstitched and a muslin storage bag. Dry clean only, and only with a cleaner who has handled Muga before. Woven to order — allow twelve weeks from confirmation.

reviews.title: The gold is the fibre, not a dye
reviews.body: I had only seen Muga in photographs and expected something brassier. It is a much deeper, quieter gold in person and it changes completely between daylight and a lit room. The mekhela came unpleated as described, which my tailor appreciated. Arrived folded in muslin with the care card.

reviews.title: Beautiful drape, stiff for the first two wears
reviews.body: Lovely weave and the kesa border is neatly finished. Muga is stiffer off the loom than I expected and it took two wears before the chador pleated properly at the shoulder. Worth knowing before a function rather than after. Four stars only for that; the silk itself is excellent.

reviews.title: Bought it as a saree rather than a drape
reviews.body: I am not from Assam and do not wear a mekhela, so a Muga saree was exactly what I wanted. Six and a quarter yards, blouse piece included, and the border is woven rather than stitched on. It has the weight of a real silk saree without being unwearable for a full evening.

reviews.title: My wedding set — worth the twelve week wait
reviews.body: Ordered in January for a November wedding and it arrived when they said it would. The kingkhap runs right across the anchal and repeats on the mekhela border, all of it woven in. The blouse piece matched the drape exactly, which is apparently the point of cutting it from the same warp.

reviews.title: Warmer than it looks
reviews.body: Handspun Eri is genuinely warm in a way I did not expect from silk — closer to a light wool. Undyed ivory goes with everything and the fringe is hand knotted, not machine finished. Washed it once by hand and it came out softer. This has replaced my winter scarf entirely.

reviews.title: Classic ivory and gold, wore it for Bihu
reviews.body: Exactly the drape you see on stage at Bihu — ivory Pat, gold zari border, nothing extra. It holds a crisp pleat which is what I wanted. Slightly less generous at the chador than my old one, so if you drape with deep pleats do check the measurements first.

reviews.title: Ordered six pairs for Bohag Bihu
reviews.body: Straightforward handwoven gamosas with the proper red border and woven buta at both ends. The listing is honest that they are cotton, which is what a gamosa should be. Packed as pairs in a kraft sleeve so I could give them without rewrapping. Washed one to check and it softened nicely.

reviews.title: Muga in a form I can actually wear to work
reviews.body: A full Muga drape was never going to leave my cupboard, so a stole made more sense. Same golden yarn, woven border, short fringe. It does read more bronze than gold under office lighting, which the description does say. Submitting this now, hopefully it clears moderation.

reviews.title: Lovely fibre, but the undyed shade was lighter than the photos
reviews.body: No complaint about the Eri itself — it is soft, matte and exactly as described in the hand. But the natural oatmeal arrived noticeably paler than the listing images, closer to cream. Support explained that undyed Eri varies by batch, which I accept, though I would have liked that flagged more clearly on the page.

reviews.title: A note on kingkhap loom time
reviews.body: From our atelier: the kingkhap on this drape is lifted thread by thread on the loom, not embroidered afterwards, which is why a single piece takes about six weeks. If a listing elsewhere offers kingkhap Muga at a fraction of this, it is almost always printed or applied work.

reviews.title: Second Muga from Meghali’s, consistent quality
reviews.body: Bought a Mekhela Chador last year and this saree in June. Same depth of gold, same finish on the border, so whatever they are doing at the Sualkuchi end is consistent between orders. Posting early before the wedding photographs are back.
